intro_en: In this lesson you will learn to point at places. You will ask and answer "Where is the bank?", "Which floor is this?" and "How much is this?". You will learn place names like railway station, bank, post office and hospital. You will learn numbers from one hundred to ten thousand. You will also learn about yen, the money of Japan. Tamil says "இங்கே / அங்கே / எங்கே" (here / there / where). Japanese has ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ. They follow the same pattern as これ・それ・あれ from the last lesson.

g03-1.explanation_en: これ・それ・あれ point at things. In the same way, ここ・そこ・あそこ point at places. ここ = where the speaker is ("here", இங்கே). そこ = near the listener ("there", அங்கே). あそこ = far from both of you ("over there", அதோ அங்கே). In Tamil, pointing words that start with "இ-" mean near, and words that start with "அ-" mean far. Japanese has a family of four starts: こ- / そ- / あ- / ど-. こちら・そちら・あちら show a direction: "this way / that way". In shops and offices they are also the polite way to say ここ・そこ・あそこ. When you introduce someone, say 「こちらは 山田さんです」. It means "This is Yamada-san" (இவர் யமாடா-சான்). It is a polite way to point at a person, like the Tamil "இவர்" (this person, with respect).
g03-1.tamil_parallel_en: இங்கே வகுப்பறை "Here is the classroom" / அங்கே வங்கி "Over there is the bank" = ここは 教室です。/ あそこは 銀行です。 The Japanese こ matches Tamil "இ" (this/here). そ and あ match "அ" (that/there). ど matches "எ" (which/where).
g03-1.formation_en: ここ / そこ / あそこ (ordinary) — こちら / そちら / あちら (polite, direction)
g03-1.pitfalls_en: When you introduce someone, 「こちらは」 is much more polite than 「この人は 田中さんです」. Say all of あそこ, not just "あそ". Don’t say it like "அச்சோ".

g03-2.explanation_en: To say where a thing or place is, use the same 「N1 は N2 です」 pattern from Lesson 1. 「銀行は あそこです」 = "The bank is over there" (வங்கி அங்கே இருக்கிறது). In Tamil too we say "வங்கி அங்கே" (bank, over there) without "இருக்கிறது" (is), right? It is the same short way. The place can be ここ・そこ・あそこ or こちら・そちら・あちら. It can also be a floor number like 五階. You can use this for people too. 「先生は 教室です」 = "The teacher is in the classroom" (ஆசிரியர் வகுப்பறையில் இருக்கிறார்).
g03-2.tamil_parallel_en: தபால் நிலையம் அங்கே "The post office is over there" = 郵便局は あそこです。 Tamil can leave out "இருக்கிறது" (is). In the same way, Japanese shows "is there" with just です.
g03-2.formation_en: N (thing / place / person) + は + place + です
g03-2.pitfalls_en: 「ここは 銀行です」 (this place is a bank) and 「銀行は ここです」 (the bank is here) are both right. But the topic (what you are talking about) is different. If the question is "Where is the bank?", make 銀行は the topic of your answer.

g03-3.explanation_en: "Where?" = どこ. The polite word is どちら. In Tamil, words that start with "எ-" ask a question. In the same way, Japanese question words start with ど-: どれ, どの, どこ, どちら. As in Tamil, the question word stays where the place goes, before です. 「駅は どこですか」 = "Where is the station?" (ரயில் நிலையம் எங்கே?). どちら can also politely mean "which way" and "which country / which company". 「お国は どちらですか」 = "Which country are you from?" (உங்கள் நாடு எது?). Asking with 何ですか here does not sound natural.
g03-3.tamil_parallel_en: ரயில் நிலையம் எங்கே? "Where is the station?" = 駅は どこですか。 / உங்கள் நாடு எது? "Which is your country?" = お国は どちらですか。 Tamil question words start with "எ-". In the same way, Japanese question words start with ど-.
g03-3.formation_en: N は どこ / どちら ですか
g03-3.pitfalls_en: どちら also means "which of the two". You will learn this in later lessons. Don’t ask "Which is your country?" as 「お国は 何ですか」. Use どちら or どこ.

g03-4.explanation_en: の has another job: it says which country or company made something. 「日本の 時計」 = a clock made in Japan (ஜப்பானியக் கடிகாரம்). 「ソニーの カメラ」 = a Sony camera (சோனி கேமரா). In Tamil we just put the words side by side, with no ending. For example, "ஜப்பான் கடிகாரம்" (Japan clock) and "சோனி கேமரா" (Sony camera). But in Japanese you must use の. To ask "made in which country…?", say 「どこの N ですか」. This is どこ + の. In the answer you can drop the noun, as in 「日本のです」. It is just like 「私のです」 in the last lesson.
g03-4.tamil_parallel_en: இது எந்த நாட்டுக் கடிகாரம்? — ஜப்பான் கடிகாரம். "Which country’s clock is this? — A Japanese clock." = これは どこの 時計ですか。— 日本の 時計です。 Tamil puts the words side by side. Japanese needs の.
g03-4.formation_en: N1 (country / company) + の + N2 ; どこの + N ですか
g03-4.pitfalls_en: Dropping の, as in 「どこ カメラ」, is wrong. Say 「どこの カメラ」. Don’t mix up "whose" (誰の) and "from which country" (どこの).

g03-5.explanation_en: To ask a price, say 「N は いくらですか」 = "How much is N?" (N என்ன விலை?). The answer is number + 円 (えん). 「百円です」 = "100 yen" (நூறு யென்). Big numbers: 百 (100), 千 (1,000), 万 (10,000). In Tamil, sounds change in "முன்னூறு" (three hundred) and "மூவாயிரம்" (three thousand). In the same way, some Japanese numbers change sound. 三百 = さんびゃく, 六百 = ろっぴゃく, 八百 = はっぴゃく, 三千 = さんぜん, 八千 = はっせん. Don’t say 10,000 as "ten thousands". Say 一万 (いちまん). 30,000 = 三万. Indians count in lakhs (லட்சம்). In the same way, Japanese people count in groups of 万. 0 = ゼロ or 零 (れい).
g03-5.tamil_parallel_en: இந்தக் குடை என்ன விலை? — ஆயிரம் யென். "How much is this umbrella? — 1,000 yen." = この傘は いくらですか。— 千円です。 Tamil sounds change, as in "முன்னூறு" (three hundred). In the same way, Japanese numbers like 三百 (さんびゃく) change sound.
g03-5.formation_en: N は いくらですか → (number) 円です ; 百 / 千 / 万
g03-5.pitfalls_en: 四円 = よえん (not よんえん). Ten thousand = 一万. Never say 「十千」. Don’t put 一 before 百 or 千 (百 = ひゃく). But you must put 一 before 万 (一万).

g03-6.explanation_en: To say a floor of a building, use number + 階 (かい). "Which floor?" = 何階 (なんがい). Note: in Japan the ground floor is 一階 (1st floor). What we call the "ground floor" in Tamil Nadu is 一階 in Japan. Our "first floor" is 二階 there. Some sounds change. 一階 = いっかい, 三階 = さんがい, 六階 = ろっかい, 八階 = はっかい (or はちかい), 十階 = じゅっかい, 何階 = なんがい. To ask "Which floor is X on?", say 「X は 何階ですか」. The answer is 「三階です」. Tamil "மூன்றாவது மாடியில்" (on the third floor) uses "-இல்" (on/in). But in Japanese, です alone is enough.
g03-6.tamil_parallel_en: தபால் நிலையம் எத்தனையாவது மாடி? — மூன்றாவது மாடி. "Which floor is the post office on? — The third floor." = 郵便局は 何階ですか。— 三階です。 Tamil adds "-இல்" (on). Japanese only needs です.
g03-6.formation_en: (number) + 階 ; N は 何階ですか
g03-6.pitfalls_en: 三階 = さんがい, 何階 = なんがい. Don’t forget that the か sound changes to が. In Japan 一階 = the ground floor. So add one to the Indian floor number.

items.L03-q01: 駅 = えき (ரயில் நிலையம், railway station). Changing き to ぎ is wrong. Adding a small っ is also wrong.
items.L03-q02: 銀行 = ぎんこう (வங்கி, bank). It ends with the long sound こう. Making it short, as ぎんこ, is wrong. Changing ぎ to き is also wrong.
items.L03-q03: 病院 = びょういん (மருத்துவமனை, hospital). びょ is one sound, with a small ょ. びよういん is 美容院 (அழகு நிலையம், beauty salon). This is a big trap!
items.L03-q04: ゆうびんきょく = 郵便局 (தபால் நிலையம், post office). Watch out for look-alikes. 使 (பயன்படுத்த, to use) is not 便. 居 is not 局. Both are traps.
items.L03-q05: たてもの = 建物 (கட்டிடம், building). 健 has an extra 亻 on the left. 勿 is only the right part of 物.
items.L03-q06: You ask "Where?" about a place: the toilet (கழிப்பறை). A name or a number does not fit the answer "over there".
items.L03-q07: The answer is a price (三万円). So the question is いくら (என்ன விலை, how much). With どこ (where), the answer would be a place.
items.L03-q08: The answer is 八階 (எட்டாவது மாடி, eighth floor). So the question is 何階 (なんがい, which floor). なんさい is the word for asking someone’s age.
items.L03-q09: To introduce someone politely, use こちら (இவர், this person). あそこ and そこ point at places, not people.
items.L03-q10: A doctor works at a 病院 (மருத்துவமனை, hospital). A doctor would not be at 銀行 (வங்கி, bank) or 交番 (போலீஸ் பூத், police box).
items.L03-q11: To ask about someone’s country politely, use どちら (எங்கே / எது, where / which). どなた means "who" (யார்). It does not fit a country.
items.L03-q12: "The bank is over there" = "The place over there is the bank" (அங்கே இருப்பது வங்கி). ここ means "here" (இங்கே). It changes the place.
items.L03-q13: "A clock made in Japan" = "This clock is Japanese" (இந்தக் கடிகாரம் ஜப்பானியது). 日本人の would mean "belonging to a Japanese person". That is about who owns it, not where it was made.
items.L03-q14: Not the second floor, but the first (ground) floor (தரை மாடி). This has the same meaning. The other choices change the floor or say "not".
items.L03-q15: The answer is a place, "over there". So the question is どこ (எங்கே, where).
items.L03-q16: "A camera from which country" = どこの カメラ. You need の to join it to the noun.
items.L03-q17: The price of a book = 三百円 (さんびゃくえん, 300 yen). かい is for floors. さい is for ages. They don’t fit a book.
items.L03-q18: After いいえ (no), "it’s not the post office" = じゃありません. Then the speaker gives the right answer: 交番です (it’s the police box).
items.L03-q19: The bank is on the second floor. The post office is on the second floor too. So "too" (-உம்) = も.
items.L03-q20: "What place is this?" (இது எந்த இடம்?) = ここは どこですか. The answer also uses ここは. So both people are in the same place.
items.L03-q21: An いくら (என்ன விலை, how much) question needs a price: 三千円 (さんぜんえん, 3,000 yen). The other choices are a floor, a number and an age.
items.L03-q22: すみません、お手洗いは 何階ですか。 — topic → question word → です → か. 何階 goes in the ★ slot.
items.L03-q23: それは どこの 時計ですか。 — どこの comes before the noun. どこの goes in the ★ slot.
items.L03-q24: あの建物は 病院じゃありません。 — あの + noun, then "not". 病院じゃ goes in the ★ slot.
items.L03-q25: ［1］ "Cameras (section) are on the fifth floor": the topic takes は. ［2］ "Japanese camera" (ஜப்பானியக் கேமரா): の shows the country. ［3］ The answer is 八階 (eighth floor). So the question is 何階.
